component.name: Kite
component.summary: KDE web browser with Firefox extension support

description.p: Kite is a web browser for the Plasma desktop, modelled on Falkon and written in Rust. It runs Firefox extensions, installed straight from addons.mozilla.org.

It blocks ads and trackers itself, keeps passwords in KWallet, fills forms, has a reader view, container tabs, and private windows that leave nothing behind. Plugins add Vim keys, mouse gestures, picture-in-picture, and integration with Plasma: media controls, KRunner, KDE Connect and the panel's download progress.

screenshot.caption: Kite on Plasma, showing its empty start page

description.p: The Flatpak follows the desktop's colors when they change while Kite is open, such as a switch between a light and a dark theme.
The extensions button's panel leaves out the Extensions section while WebExtensions are switched off.
The About dialog shows Kite's icon again.
Kite as a Flatpak, from a repository that keeps it updated. Its application ID is now io.github.n4n0gh.kite.

Private windows can have purple window chrome. Vim keys no longer go quiet with the keyboard in a widget frame or a picker. Profiles can be renamed from the picker. A YouTube Download plugin saves videos with yt-dlp. The built-in blocker works like uBlock Origin, with an element picker.
Settings laid out as in System Settings, with Apply. A user agent per site. A log file and crash reports. Forms act only on trusted clicks, submits and Enter.
Pointer lock for pages, on Wayland.
